title.zh: 卷八十七 列傳第七十五: 酷吏
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第七十五: 酷吏 Volume 87 Biographies 75: Cruel Officials

sentences.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 子神 張赦提 趙霸 崔暹 邸珍 田式 燕榮 元弘嗣 王文同

translations.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zishen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xian, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, Wang Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou; Hu Ni; Li Hongzhi; Zishen; Zhang Sheti; Zhao Ba; Cui Xian; Di Zhen; Tian Shi; Yan Rong; Yuan Hongsi; Wang Wentong.

sentences.zh: 夫為國之體有四焉：一曰仁義，二曰禮制，三曰法令，四曰刑罰。

translations.literal: Now the structure of governing a state has four parts: first, benevolence and righteousness; second, ritual institutions; third, laws and ordinances; fourth, punishments and penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The framework of statecraft rests on four pillars: benevolence and righteousness, ritual order, statutes, and penal law.

sentences.zh: 仁義、禮制，教之本也；

translations.literal: Benevolence, righteousness, and ritual institutions are the root of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence, righteousness, and ritual form the foundation of civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 法令、刑罰，教之末也。

translations.literal: Laws, ordinances, punishments, and penalties are the branch-tips of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and punishments are only the outermost tools of instruction.

sentences.zh: 無本不立，無末不成。

translations.literal: Without the root one cannot stand; without the branch-tips one cannot complete.
translations.idiomatic: Without roots nothing stands; without branches nothing is finished.

sentences.zh: 然教化遠而刑罰近，可以助化而不可以專行，可以立威而不可以繁用。

translations.literal: Yet transforming instruction is distant while punishments and penalties are near; they can assist transformation but cannot be practiced alone, can establish awe but cannot be used in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Moral transformation works slowly and from afar, whereas punishment strikes close at hand: it may reinforce civilizing rule but must not replace it, and it may inspire awe but must not be wielded constantly.

sentences.zh: 老子曰：「其政察察，其人缺缺。

translations.literal: Laozi said: "When government is scrutinizing, the people are deficient."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, "When government grows ever more exacting, the people grow ever more diminished."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「法令滋章，盜賊多有。

translations.literal: " He also said: "When laws and ordinances multiply in chapters, robbers and bandits abound."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When statutes multiply clause by clause, thieves and outlaws multiply in turn."

sentences.zh: 」然則，令之煩苛，吏之嚴酷，不可致化，百世可知。

translations.literal: " Thus then, when ordinances are vexatious and severe and officials are harsh and cruel, transformation cannot be achieved—a truth knowable for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that oppressive laws and pitiless magistrates cannot bring order; that lesson holds for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 考覽前載，有時而用之矣。

translations.literal: Examining former records, there have been times when they were employed.
translations.idiomatic: A review of earlier chronicles shows that such methods were sometimes deployed.

sentences.zh: 昔秦任獄吏，赭衣滿道。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin employed prison clerks, and convicts in ochre robes filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Qin entrusted power to jailers until the highways swarmed with prisoners in russet garb.

sentences.zh: 漢革其風，矯枉過正，禁綱疏闊，遂漏吞舟。

translations.literal: Han reformed that wind, straightening the bent past excess, until prohibitions and nets grew slack and wide, and even a vessel that could swallow a boat leaked through.
translations.idiomatic: The Han overturned that climate but overcorrected: legal restraints grew so loose that even great malefactors slipped through the net.

sentences.zh: 故大奸巨猾，犯義悖禮。

translations.literal: Therefore great traitors and cunning villains violated righteousness and rebelled against ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thus grand conspirators and cunning rogues defied duty and scorned propriety.

sentences.zh: 郅都、甯成之倫，猛氣奮發，摧拉凶邪，一切以救時弊。

translations.literal: Men such as Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, with fierce spirit roused, crushed vicious evil, doing everything to remedy the ills of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhi Du and Ning Cheng rose with savage energy, broke violent wrongdoers, and bent every expedient to the maladies of their day.

sentences.zh: 雖乖教義，或有所取焉。

translations.literal: Although they departed from the doctrine of instruction, there was perhaps something to be taken from them.
translations.idiomatic: Though they strayed from humane governance, their methods were not wholly without merit.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯之徒，前書編之《酷吏》。

translations.literal: The party of Yu Luohou and the like were compiled in the former histories under "Cruel Officials."
translations.idiomatic: The circle of Yu Luohou and his kind appear in earlier histories in the chapter on cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 或因餘緒，或以微功，遭遇時來，忝竊高位。

translations.literal: Some by residual connections, some by slight merit, encountered the times and came forward, undeservedly usurping high position.
translations.idiomatic: Some rode old connections, others a minor deed; when fortune smiled they climbed to rank they did not deserve.

sentences.zh: 肆其褊性，多行無禮，君子小人，咸罹其毒。

translations.literal: They unleashed their narrow natures, often acting without ritual; gentlemen and commoners alike suffered their poison.
translations.idiomatic: They indulged their cramped temperaments, trampled propriety, and poisoned noble and humble alike.

sentences.zh: 凡所蒞職，莫不懍然。

translations.literal: Wherever they took office, none failed to tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Every jurisdiction they entered trembled before them.

sentences.zh: 居其下者，視之如蛇虺；

translations.literal: Those beneath them regarded them as serpents and vipers;
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates looked on them as serpents and asps;

sentences.zh: 過其境者，逃之如寇仇。

translations.literal: those who passed through their territories fled as from a bitter foe.
translations.idiomatic: travelers through their districts fled as from mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 與人之恩，心非好善；

translations.literal: when they showed others favor, their hearts were not bent on goodness;
translations.idiomatic: When they showed favor, their hearts were not moved by goodness;

sentences.zh: 加人之罪，事非疾惡。

translations.literal: when they heaped guilt on others, the affair was not born of hatred of evil.
translations.idiomatic: when they piled on guilt, it was not born of zeal against wickedness.

sentences.zh: 其所笞辱，多在無辜。

translations.literal: Those whom they flogged and humiliated were mostly innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those they flogged and humiliated were innocent.

sentences.zh: 察其所為，豺狼之不若也。

translations.literal: Examining what they did, they were not even the equal of wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by their deeds, they fell short of wolves.

sentences.zh: 其禁奸除猾，殆與郅、寧之倫異乎。

translations.literal: Their prohibiting treachery and removing rascals scarcely differed from the class of Zhi and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Their supposed purging of traitors and rogues had little in common with the work of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng.

sentences.zh: 君子賤之，故編於《酷吏》。

translations.literal: Gentlemen despised them; therefore they were compiled in "Cruel Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle despised them, and so they were gathered into the chapter on cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 魏有于洛侯、胡泥、李洪之、高遵、張赦提、羊祉、崔暹、酈道元、穀楷。

translations.literal: Wei had Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Wei were Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xian, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai.

sentences.zh: 齊有邸珍、宋游道、盧斐、畢義云。

translations.literal: Qi had Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Qi were Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun.

sentences.zh: 《周書》不立此篇。

translations.literal: The Zhou History does not establish this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Zhou does not include such a chapter.

sentences.zh: 《隋書》有庫狄士文、田式、燕榮、趙仲卿、崔弘度、元弘嗣、王文同。

translations.literal: The Sui History has Kudil Shiwen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Zhao Zhongqing, Cui Hongdu, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Sui lists Kudil Shiwen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Zhao Zhongqing, Cui Hongdu, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong.

sentences.zh: 今檢高遵、羊祉、酈道元、谷楷、宋游道、盧斐、畢義雲、庫狄士文、趙仲卿、崔弘度各從其家傳，其餘並列於此云。

translations.literal: Now examining Gao Zun, Yang Zhi, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun, Kudil Shiwen, Zhao Zhongqing, and Cui Hongdu—each is taken from his family biography; the rest are gathered here together.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zun, Yang Zhi, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun, Kudil Shiwen, Zhao Zhongqing, and Cui Hongdu are each treated in their family biographies; the remainder are collected in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯

translations.literal: Yu Luohou
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou

sentences.zh: 于洛侯，代人也。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 為秦州刺史，貪酷安忍。

translations.literal: As prefect of Qinzhou he was greedy, cruel, and calmly ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Qinzhou he was greedy, pitiless, and calmly cruel.

sentences.zh: 部人富熾奪人呂勝脛纏一具，洛侯輒鞭富熾一百，截其右腕。

translations.literal: A man of his district, Fu Chi, seized a pair of shin-guards from Lü Sheng; Luohou at once flogged Fu Chi one hundred strokes and cut off his right wrist.
translations.idiomatic: When a local man named Fu Chi seized a pair of greaves from Lü Sheng, Luohou had him flogged a hundred times and struck off his right wrist.

sentences.zh: 百姓王隴客刺殺人王羌奴、王愈二人，依律罪死。

translations.literal: The commoner Wang Longke had stabbed and killed Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu; by law the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Wang Longke had murdered Wang Qiangnu and Wang Yu; by statute the offense deserved death.

sentences.zh: 而洛侯生拔隴客舌，刺其本，並刺胸腹二十餘瘡。

translations.literal: Yet Luohou tore out Longke's tongue alive, pierced its root, and likewise pierced more than twenty wounds in chest and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou instead ripped out Longke's tongue alive, stabbed its root, and drove more than twenty blades into his chest and belly.

sentences.zh: 隴客不堪苦痛，隨刀戰動。

translations.literal: Longke could not bear the agony and jerked with each cut of the knife.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure the pain, Longke convulsed with every stroke of the blade.

sentences.zh: 乃立四柱，磔其手足。

translations.literal: He then set up four pillars and dismembered his limbs upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou then erected four posts and spread-eagled him upon them.

sentences.zh: 命將絕，始斬其首，支解四體，分懸道路。

translations.literal: When his breath was nearly gone, he at last beheaded him, quartered the body, and hung the pieces along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Only when life was almost gone did he behead him, quarter the corpse, and hang the pieces along the highway.

sentences.zh: 見者無不傷楚歎愕。

translations.literal: None who saw it failed to grieve, ache, sigh, and stare in horror.
translations.idiomatic: Every witness grieved, shuddered, and stared in horror.

sentences.zh: 百姓王元壽等一時反叛。

translations.literal: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rose in revolt all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners led by Wang Yuanshou rose in revolt at once.

sentences.zh: 有司糾劾，孝文詔使者於州常刑人處，宣告兵人，然後斬洛侯以謝百姓。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached him; Emperor Xiaowen ordered an envoy to proclaim the matter to the troops at the usual place of execution in the province, and then beheaded Luohou to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him; Emperor Xiaowen sent an envoy to the province's usual execution ground to announce the case to the soldiery, then beheaded Luohou to appease the populace.

sentences.zh: 胡泥，代人也。

translations.literal: Hu Ni was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ni came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 曆官至司衛監，賜爵永成侯。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Director of Palace Guards and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Palace Guards and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 泥率勒禁中，不憚豪貴。

translations.literal: Ni led and restrained those within the forbidden precincts and did not fear the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace precincts he enforced discipline without fearing the mighty.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書叔孫侯頭應內直而闕於一時，泥以法繩之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Shusun Houtou, who should have been on inner duty, was absent for a time; Ni bound him by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Shusun Houtou failed a turn of inner duty, Ni prosecuted him under the law.

sentences.zh: 侯頭恃寵，遂與口諍。

translations.literal: Houtou relied on favor and thereupon quarreled with him by word.
translations.idiomatic: Houtou, trusting in imperial favor, quarreled with him openly.

sentences.zh: 孝文聞而嘉焉，賜泥衣服一襲，出為幽州刺史，假范陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen heard of it and commended this; he bestowed on Ni one suit of clothing and sent him out as prefect of Youzhou, with acting authority over Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen praised his conduct, granted him a suit of robes, and appointed him prefect of Youzhou with acting authority over Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 以北平陽尼碩學，遂表薦之。

translations.literal: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a profound scholar, he memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the eminent scholar Yang Ni of Beiping in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 轉為定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Dingzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 以暴虐，刑罰酷濫，受納貨賄，徽還戮之。

translations.literal: For violence and cruelty, excessive and wanton punishments, and accepting bribes, he was recalled and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled for savage rule, wanton punishments, and bribery, he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 將就法，孝文臨太華殿引見，遣侍臣宣詔責之，遂就家賜盡。

translations.literal: As he was about to suffer the law, Emperor Xiaowen came to the Taihua Hall to receive him, sent attendants to proclaim an edict rebuking him, and then granted him death at home.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of execution Emperor Xiaowen received him at Taihua Hall, had attendants read out a rebuking edict, and allowed him to die by suicide at home.

sentences.zh: 李洪之

translations.literal: Li Hongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhi

sentences.zh: 李洪之，本名文通，恆農人也。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhi, original name Wentong, was a man of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhi, born Wentong, came from Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，晚乃還俗。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; only late did he return to the laity.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his youth as a monk and returned to lay life only in later years.

sentences.zh: 真君中，為狄道護軍，賜爵安陽男。

translations.literal: In the Zhenjun era he was Protector-General of Didao and enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector-General of Didao and was enfeoffed Baron of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 會永昌王仁隨太武南征，得元後姊妹二人，洪之潛相餉遺，結為兄弟，遂便如親。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Yongchang Ren followed Emperor Taiwu on the southern campaign and obtained two sisters of the Lady Yuan; Hongzhi secretly made gifts to them, entered brotherhood with them, and thereupon became as close as kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yongchang Ren followed Emperor Taiwu south and took two sisters of Lady Yuan, Hongzhi secretly courted them with gifts, swore brotherhood, and treated them as kin.

sentences.zh: 頗得元後在南兄弟名字，乃改名洪之。

translations.literal: He came to know rather well the names of the Lady Yuan's brothers in the south and thereupon changed his name to Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the names of Lady Yuan's brothers in the south, he renamed himself Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 及仁坐事誅，元後入宮，得幸於文成，生獻文。

translations.literal: When Ren was executed for an offense, the Lady Yuan entered the palace, won favor from Emperor Wencheng, and bore Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: After Ren was executed, Lady Yuan entered the palace, won Emperor Wencheng's favor, and bore Emperor Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 元後臨崩，太后問其親，因言洪之為兄。

translations.literal: As the Lady Yuan lay dying, the empress dowager asked about her kin, and she said Hongzhi was her brother.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed Lady Yuan told the empress dowager that Hongzhi was her brother.

sentences.zh: 與相訣經日，具條列南方諸兄珍之等，手以付洪之。

translations.literal: They took leave of one another for days; she fully listed her southern brothers Zhenzhi and the rest and handed the list to Hongzhi in her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: They parted over many days while she itemized her southern kin, including Zhenzhi, and placed the list in Hongzhi's own hand.

sentences.zh: 遂號為獻文親舅。

translations.literal: He was thereupon styled the maternal uncle of Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he was treated as Emperor Xianwen's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 太安中，珍之等兄弟至都，與洪之相見，敘元後平生故事，計長幼為昆季。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era Zhenzhi and his brothers reached the capital; meeting Hongzhi, they recounted the Lady Yuan's life story and reckoned seniority to become sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tai'an era Zhenzhi and his brothers reached the capital, met Hongzhi, recounted Lady Yuan's life, and by reckoned seniority became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 以外戚為河內太守，進爵任城侯，威儀一同刺史。

translations.literal: By virtue of his maternal kinship he became prefect of Henei, advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, with insignia equal to a provincial inspector.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial kin he became prefect of Henei and Marquis of Rencheng, with regalia equal to a provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 河內北連上党，南接武牢，地險人悍，數為劫害，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: Henei bordered Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south; the land was rugged and the people fierce, and robbery was frequent—district elders could not suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: Henei, rugged and fierce, linked Shangdang in the north to Wulao in the south; banditry flourished beyond any magistrate's control.

sentences.zh: 洪之至郡，嚴設科防，募斬賊者，便加重賞，勤勸務本，盜賊止息。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi reached the commandery he sternly set up regulations and defenses, recruited those who beheaded robbers and at once doubled the reward, diligently urged return to the fundamentals, and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At his arrival he imposed strict defenses, paid lavish bounties for the heads of robbers, urged the people back to honest labor, and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 誅鋤奸黨，過為酷虐。

translations.literal: In rooting out treacherous factions he went beyond measure into cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in purging factions he exceeded all bounds of cruelty.

sentences.zh: 後為懷州刺史，封漢郡公，徵拜內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he was prefect of Huaizhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Han Commandery, and summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Huaizhou, was enfeoffed Duke of Han Commandery, and was summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 河西羌胡領部落反叛，獻文親征，命洪之與侍中、東郡王陸定總統諸軍。

translations.literal: When the Qiang and Hu of Hexi led their tribes in rebellion, Emperor Xianwen campaigned in person and ordered Hongzhi, together with the Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Dongjun Lu Ding, to command all armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi tribes rebelled, Emperor Xianwen marched in person and placed Hongzhi with Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Ding, Prince of Dongjun, over the combined armies.

sentences.zh: 輿駕至并州，詔洪之為河西都將，討山胡。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bingzhou, Hongzhi was ordered general of Hexi to subdue the mountain Hu.
translations.idiomatic: At Bingzhou he was appointed general of Hexi to subdue the mountain Hu.

sentences.zh: 皆保險距戰，洪之築壘於石樓南白雞原以對之。

translations.literal: All held the passes and resisted; Hongzhi built ramparts on the White Chicken Plain south of Shilou to confront them.
translations.idiomatic: They held the passes; Hongzhi built fortifications on the White Chicken Plain south of Shilou to confront them.

sentences.zh: 時諸將悉欲進攻，洪之乃開以大信，聽其復業。

translations.literal: At the time all the generals wished to attack; Hongzhi instead opened great trust and allowed them to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: While other generals urged attack, Hongzhi offered generous terms and let them resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 胡人遂降。

translations.literal: The Hu thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 獻文嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen praised the outcome.

sentences.zh: 遷拜尚書、外都大官。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Minister and Grand Director of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister and Grand Director of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 後為使持節、安南將軍、秦、益二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, and prefect of Qin and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held the staff of authority as General Who Pacifies the South and governed Qin and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 至任，設禁奸之制。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he established regulations for prohibiting wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he imposed stern anti-crime regulations.

sentences.zh: 有帶刃行者，罪與劫同。

translations.literal: Whoever went about bearing a blade was guilty as for robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone found carrying a blade was punished as a robber.

sentences.zh: 輕重品格，各有條章。

translations.literal: Grades of severity and leniency each had their articles.
translations.idiomatic: Each degree of offense had its written rule.

sentences.zh: 於是大饗州中豪傑長老，示之法制。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly feasted the commandery's eminent men and elders and displayed the laws to them.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted the commandery's leading families and elders and displayed the code before them.

sentences.zh: 乃夜密遣騎分部覆諸要路，有犯禁者，輒捉送州，宣告斬決。

translations.literal: Then by night he secretly sent horsemen in divisions to cover the key roads; whoever violated the prohibitions was seized and sent to the prefecture, proclaimed, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That night he secretly posted horsemen on every vital road; violators were seized, brought to the prefecture, and beheaded after public announcement.

sentences.zh: 其中枉見殺害者，至有百數。

translations.literal: Among them those wrongly killed reached as many as a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The wrongly executed numbered as many as a hundred.

sentences.zh: 赤葩渴郎羌深居山谷，雖相羈縻，王人罕到。

translations.literal: The Chipa Kelang Qiang dwelt deep in mountain valleys; though nominally under restraint, royal agents rarely reached them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chipa Kelang Qiang lived deep in the mountains; though nominally subject, imperial agents seldom arrived.

sentences.zh: 洪之芟山為道，廣十餘步，示以軍行之勢。

translations.literal: Hongzhi cut down mountains to make a road more than ten paces wide, displaying the momentum of military march.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi cut a road more than ten paces wide through the mountains to display the might of an army on the march.

sentences.zh: 乃興軍臨其境，山人驚駭。

translations.literal: He then raised an army and pressed into their territory; the mountain people were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He marched in force; the mountaineers were terrified.

sentences.zh: 洪之將數十騎至其里閭，撫其妻子，問所疾苦，因資遺之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi took several dozen horsemen to their hamlets, comforted their wives and children, asked their hardships, and bestowed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He rode in with a few dozen horsemen, comforted wives and children, inquired after their hardships, and gave gifts.

sentences.zh: 眾羌喜悅，求編課調，所入十倍於常。

translations.literal: The Qiang masses rejoiced, sought enrollment for tax and corvée, and the intake was ten times the usual.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang rejoiced, sought enrollment for tax and corvée, and revenue rose tenfold.

sentences.zh: 洪之善禦戎夷，頗有威惠，而刻害之聲，聞於朝野。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was skilled at controlling the barbarians and had considerable authority and kindness, yet the sound of his harsh cruelty was heard at court and in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He governed frontier peoples with skill and a measure of benevolence, yet reports of his cruelty reached court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 初，洪之微時妻張氏，亦聰強婦人，自貧賤至富貴，多所補益，有男女幾十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hongzhi was still obscure his wife Lady Zhang was also a clever, forceful woman; from poverty and baseness to wealth and honor she contributed much, and they had several tens of sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days his wife Lady Zhang was herself clever and forceful; from poverty to power she aided him greatly, and they reared several dozen children.

sentences.zh: 洪之後得劉芳從姊，重之，疏張氏。

translations.literal: Later Hongzhi obtained a cousin of Liu Fang and favored her, estranging Lady Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took a cousin of Liu Fang, favored her, and grew distant from Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 亦多所產育。

translations.literal: She too bore many children.
translations.idiomatic: The second wife bore many children as well.

sentences.zh: 為兩宅別居，偏厚劉室，由是二妻妒競，兩宅母子，往來如仇。

translations.literal: He set up two separate residences; favoring the Liu household, the two wives competed in jealousy, and the mothers and sons of the two houses dealt with one another like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He maintained two households, lavished favor on the Liu line, and the two wives' factions met like sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 及蒞西州，以劉自隨。

translations.literal: When he went to the western province he took the Liu woman with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up office in the west he brought the Liu wife with him.

sentences.zh: 洪之素非廉清，每有受納。

translations.literal: Hongzhi had never been honest and clean; he always accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was never honest; he always took bribes.

sentences.zh: 時孝文始建祿制，法禁嚴峻，遂鎖洪之赴京，親臨太華，庭集群臣數之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowen was first establishing the salary system and legal prohibitions were severe; Hongzhi was shackled and sent to the capital; the emperor came in person to Taihua, assembled the ministers in court, and counted his offenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen instituted the salary system with stern law, Hongzhi was shackled and brought to the capital; the emperor assembled the ministers at Taihua Hall and enumerated his crimes.

sentences.zh: 以其大臣，聽在家自裁。

translations.literal: Because he was a great minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister he was allowed to die by suicide at home.

sentences.zh: 洪之志性慷慨，多所堪忍。

translations.literal: Hongzhi's disposition was generous and he bore much.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was by nature magnanimous and enduring.

sentences.zh: 疹病炙療，艾炷圍將二寸，首足十餘處，一時俱下，言笑自若，接賓不輟。

translations.literal: When moxibustion treated his rash illness, moxa cones nearly two inches around were placed at more than ten spots on head and feet, all applied at once; he spoke and laughed as usual and did not cease receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: During moxibustion for a skin ailment, cones nearly two inches across were burned at more than ten points on head and feet all at once; he laughed and talked as usual and never stopped receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 及臨盡，沐浴衣幍，防卒扶持，出入遍巡家庭，如是再三，泣歎良久，乃臥而引藥。

translations.literal: When he was about to die, he bathed, dressed in cap and robe, had guards support him, and went in and out through the whole household three times, weeping and sighing for a long while, then lay down and took poison.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he bathed, dressed in cap and robe, had guards escort him through every room of the house three times, wept long, then lay down and took poison.

sentences.zh: 始洪之托為元後兄，公私自同外戚。

translations.literal: At first Hongzhi had claimed to be the Lady Yuan's brother, and in public and private he was the same as other maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had passed himself off as Lady Yuan's brother and enjoyed the privileges of imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 至此罪後，孝文乃稍對百官辯其誣假。

translations.literal: After this offense Emperor Xiaowen gradually explained to the assembled officials that the claim was false.
translations.idiomatic: After his fall Emperor Xiaowen gradually explained to the court that the kinship was a fraud.

sentences.zh: 而諸李猶善相視，恩紀如親。

translations.literal: Yet the various Lis still treated one another kindly, their bonds of favor like kin.
translations.idiomatic: Even so the Li clan continued to treat one another with familial warmth.

sentences.zh: 洪之始見元後，計年為兄。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi first met the Lady Yuan, he reckoned their years and called himself her elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When he first met Lady Yuan he reckoned their ages and styled himself her elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及珍之等至，洪之以元後素定長幼，其呼拜坐，皆如家人。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi, because the Lady Yuan had long since fixed seniority, made his salutations and seating all as within a family.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhi arrived, Hongzhi—Lady Yuan having long fixed their seniority—greeted and seated them exactly as kin.

sentences.zh: 暮年，數延攜之宴飲。

translations.literal: In his later years he often invited them to banquets.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he often invited them to feasts.

sentences.zh: 醉酣之後，時或言及本末，洪之則起而加敬，笑語自若。

translations.literal: After wine had thoroughly warmed them, they would sometimes speak of how it all began; Hongzhi would rise and add respect, laughing and talking as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When wine ran deep they sometimes recalled how the bond began; Hongzhi would rise to show respect yet laugh as before.

sentences.zh: 富貴赫奕，舅戚之家。

translations.literal: Wealth and glory blazed; he was kin to the imperial consort's house.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and glory surrounded him as kin to the imperial consort's house.

sentences.zh: 遂棄宗，專附珍之等。

translations.literal: He thereupon abandoned his clan and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his own clan and clung chiefly to Zhenzhi's circle.

sentences.zh: 後頗存振本屬，而猶不顯然。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat revived support for his native lineage, yet still not openly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he somewhat aided his native kin, though never openly.

sentences.zh: 劉氏四子。

translations.literal: Lady Liu bore four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu bore four sons.

sentences.zh: 張赦提

translations.literal: Zhang Sheti
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheti

sentences.zh: 張赦提，中山安喜人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheti was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheti came from Anxi in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 性雄武，有規畫。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold in martial spirit and had plans and measures.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold, martial, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 初為武卉中郎。

translations.literal: At first he was a martial cadet in the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a martial cadet in the guard.

sentences.zh: 時京畿盜魁，首稱豹子、彪子，並善弓馬，於靈丘、應門間聚為劫害。

translations.literal: At the time the chief bandits of the capital region were known as Baozi and Biaozi; both were skilled with bow and horse and between Lingqiu and Yingmen gathered to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's worst bandits, Baozi and Biaozi, were master archers and horsemen who raided between Lingqiu and Yingmen.

sentences.zh: 至乃斬人首，射其口，刺人臍，引腸繞樹而共射之，以為戲笑。

translations.literal: They even cut off men's heads, shot arrows into their mouths, stabbed their navels, drew out the intestines, wrapped them around trees, and shot at them together for sport.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off heads, shot arrows through mouths, stabbed bellies, looped entrails around trees, and used the corpses for archery sport.

sentences.zh: 其暴酷如此。

translations.literal: Their violence and cruelty were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Their cruelty reached such extremes.

sentences.zh: 軍騎掩捕，久弗能獲，行者患焉。

translations.literal: Cavalry swept in to seize them but for a long time could not capture them; travelers were afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial cavalry hunted them for years without success, and travelers lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 赦提為逐賊軍將，未幾而獲彪子、豹子及其黨與，盡送京師，斬於闕下，自是清靜。

translations.literal: Sheti served as a pursuing-bandit general and before long captured Baozi, Biaozi, and their gang, sending them all to the capital to be beheaded below the gate; thereafter there was peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti, appointed to pursue them, soon captured Baozi, Biaozi, and their band, sent them to the capital for execution at the gate, and the roads grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 其靈丘羅思祖，宗門豪溢，家處隘險，多止亡命，與之為劫。

translations.literal: At Lingqiu, Luo Sizu of the Luo clan had a clan gate overflowing with wealth; his house lay in narrow, perilous terrain, and many fugitives stopped there and joined him in robbery.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingqiu the Luo clansman Sizu was extravagantly rich; his house sat in rugged terrain where fugitives gathered and robbed with him.

sentences.zh: 獻文怒之，孥戮其家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was enraged and exterminated his family to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen, enraged, exterminated his entire family.

sentences.zh: 而思祖家黨，相率寇盜。

translations.literal: Yet Sizu's clansmen and partisans in succession raided and robbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sizu's kin and followers turned to banditry in waves.

sentences.zh: 赦提募求捕逐。

translations.literal: Sheti recruited men to hunt and pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti recruited men to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 以赦提為遊徼軍將，前後擒獲，殺之略盡。

translations.literal: As roaming patrol general, before and after he captured and killed them nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: As roaming patrol general he captured and killed them until scarcely any remained.

sentences.zh: 因此，濫有屠害，尤為忍酷。

translations.literal: Because of this he wantonly slaughtered and was especially cruel and ruthless.
translations.idiomatic: In the process he slaughtered indiscriminately and grew especially pitiless.

sentences.zh: 既資前稱，又藉此功，除幽州刺史，假安喜侯。

translations.literal: Having the earlier reputation and also relying on this merit, he was appointed prefect of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Acting Marquis of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of that fame and those deeds he became prefect of Youzhou and Acting Marquis of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 赦提克己厲約，遂有清稱。

translations.literal: Sheti restrained himself and tightened discipline, and thereupon gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he tightened his conduct and won a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 後頗縱妻段氏，多有受納。

translations.literal: Later he rather indulged his wife Lady Duan, who often accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan, who took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 命僧尼因事通請，貪虐流聞。

translations.literal: He ordered monks and nuns to use affairs to gain access and plead; greed and cruelty spread in report.
translations.idiomatic: He let monks and nuns plead through him for favors; greed and cruelty became notorious.

sentences.zh: 中散李真香出使幽州，採訪牧守政績。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang went on mission to Youzhou to investigate the achievements and governance of prefects and protectors.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang inspected Youzhou to review prefects' conduct.

sentences.zh: 真香驗案其罪，赦提懼死欲逃。

translations.literal: Zhenxiang verified and prosecuted his crimes; Sheti, fearing death, wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxiang verified his crimes; Sheti, fearing execution, tried to flee.

sentences.zh: 其妻姑為太尉、東陽王丕妻，恃丕親貴，自許詣丕申訴求助，謂赦提曰：「當為訴理，幸得申雪，願寬憂，不為異計。

translations.literal: His wife's aunt was wife to the Grand Commandant and Prince of Dongyang, Wang Pi; relying on Pi's kin favor, she promised to go to Pi to plead for help, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case and hope to clear you; put aside your worry and do not take other measures."
translations.idiomatic: His wife's aunt was wife to Grand Commandant Wang Pi, Prince of Dongyang; trusting Pi's influence, she promised to plead for him: "I will clear your name—set your mind at ease and attempt nothing rash."

sentences.zh: 」赦提以此，差自解慰。

translations.literal: Sheti thereby somewhat relieved his anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Sheti took some comfort from this.

sentences.zh: 段乃陳列：真香昔嘗因假而過幽州，知赦提有好牛，從索不果。

translations.literal: Lady Duan then set forth: Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave and knew Sheti had a fine ox; he asked for it and did not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan then claimed Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave, coveted Sheti's fine ox, and been refused.

sentences.zh: 令台使止挾前事，故威逼部下，拷楚過極，橫以無辜，證成誣罪。

translations.literal: She ordered the imperial envoy to seize on the earlier affair; therefore he coerced his subordinates, torture exceeded all bounds, and innocence was forced into false guilt.
translations.idiomatic: She alleged the envoy was settling that old grudge, coerced subordinates, tortured beyond measure, and framed the innocent.

sentences.zh: 執事恐有不盡，使駕部令趙秦州重往究訊，事狀如前，處赦提大辟。

translations.literal: Those in charge feared the case was incomplete and sent Director of the Stables Zhao Qinzhou to investigate again; the facts were as before, and Sheti was sentenced to the great penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an incomplete case, the court sent Director of the Stables Zhao Qinzhou to reinvestigate; the facts stood, and Sheti was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔賜死於第。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen ordered him granted death at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered him to die at home.

sentences.zh: 將就盡，命妻而責之曰：「貪濁穢吾者卿也，又安吾而不得免禍，九泉之下，當為仇仇矣。」

translations.literal: As he was about to perish, he summoned his wife and rebuked her: "It was you who with greed and filth ruined me, and you could not save me from disaster; in the realm below the yellow springs we shall be bitter foes."
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of death he summoned his wife and said, "Your greed ruined me, yet you could not save me from ruin; below the yellow springs we shall be bitter foes."

sentences.zh: 又有華山太守趙霸，酷暴非理。

translations.literal: There was also Zhao Ba, prefect of Huashan, cruel and violent beyond reason.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Ba, prefect of Huashan, cruel beyond reason.

sentences.zh: 大使崔光奏霸云：「不遵憲度，威虐任情，至乃手擊吏人，僚屬奔走，不可以君人字下，納之軌物。

translations.literal: Grand envoy Cui Guang memorialized against Ba, saying: "He does not follow the statutes, acts with awe and cruelty as he pleases, even personally striking clerks and subordinates until they flee; he cannot be kept beneath the ruler's character and brought within the measure of things."
translations.idiomatic: Grand envoy Cui Guang reported that Ba ignored law, ruled by terror, beat clerks until they fled, and was unfit to hold office.

sentences.zh: 輒禁止在州。

translations.literal: He was forthwith detained in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He was detained in the province.

sentences.zh: 」詔免所居官。

translations.literal: An edict removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 崔暹，字元欽，本雲清河東武城人也，世家於滎陽、潁川之間。

translations.literal: Cui Xian, style Yuanqin, was originally from Dongwucheng in Qinghe of Yun, his family having dwelt for generations between Xingyang and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian, styled Yuanqin, came from Dongwucheng in Yun's Qinghe; his family had long lived between Xingyang and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 性猛酷，少仁恕，奸猾好利，能事勢家。

translations.literal: By nature fierce and cruel, in youth lacking benevolence and forgiveness, crafty and slippery, fond of profit, able to serve powerful houses.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce, cruel, unforgiving, crafty, greedy, and adept at courting the powerful.

sentences.zh: 初以秀才累遷南袞州刺史，盜用官瓦，贓汙狼籍，為御史中尉李平所糾，免官。

translations.literal: At first as a cultivated talent he rose through repeated promotions to Inspector of Southern Gun, stole official tiles, and his bribes lay in heaps; he was impeached by the Inspector of Cases Li Ping and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Rising as a cultivated talent to Inspector of Southern Gun, he stole official tiles and amassed bribes until Inspector of Cases Li Ping impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 後行豫州事，尋即真。

translations.literal: Later he acted for Yuzhou affairs and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted for Yuzhou and soon held the post in full.

sentences.zh: 遣子析戶，分隸三縣，廣占田宅，藏匿官奴，障吝陂葦，侵盜公私，為御史中尉王顯所彈，免官。

translations.literal: He sent his son to divide the household register among three counties, broadly occupying fields and residences, concealing official slaves, obstructing public ponds and reeds, and encroaching on public and private property; he was impeached by the Inspector of Cases Wang Xian and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He registered his son across three counties, seized broad estates, hid official slaves, monopolized ponds and reeds, and encroached on public and private lands until Inspector of Cases Wang Xian impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 後累遷瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he rose through repeated promotions to Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 貪暴安忍，人庶患之。

translations.literal: Greedy, violent, and calmly ruthless, the people suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, violent, and pitiless, he made the people suffer.

sentences.zh: 嘗出獵州北，單騎至人村，有汲水婦人，暹令飲馬，因問曰：「崔瀛州何如？

translations.literal: Once when he went hunting north of the province with a single horse to a human village, there was a woman drawing water; Xian ordered his horse to drink and asked: "How is Inspector Cui of Yingzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Once hunting north of the province he rode alone to a village where a woman drew water; he made his horse drink and asked, "How is Inspector Cui of Yingzhou?"

sentences.zh: 」婦人不知是暹，答曰：「百姓何罪！

translations.literal: The woman did not know it was Xian and answered: "What crime have the people committed!"
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing him, she answered, "What crime have the people committed!"

sentences.zh: 得如此癩兒刺史。

translations.literal: To get such a scabby-son inspector."
translations.idiomatic: To get such a scabby wretch for an inspector."

sentences.zh: 」暹默然而去。

translations.literal: Xian went away in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Xian left without a word.

sentences.zh: 以不稱職，被解還京。

translations.literal: Because he was unfit for office, he was dismissed and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Judged unfit for office, he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 武川鎮反，詔暹為都督，李崇討之。

translations.literal: When Wuchuan Garrison rebelled, an edict made Xian commander; Li Chong attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchuan Garrison rebelled he was made commander under Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 違崇節度，為賊所敗，單騎潛還。

translations.literal: He violated Chong's commands, was defeated by the rebels, and returned alone on a single horse in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He disobeyed Chong, was routed, and slipped back alone on one horse.

sentences.zh: 禁於廷尉，以女妓園田貨元叉獲免。

translations.literal: He was detained by the Minister of Justice; with female entertainers, gardens, and fields he bribed Yuan Cha and was released.
translations.idiomatic: Detained by the Minister of Justice, he bribed Yuan Cha with courtesans, gardens, and fields and went free.

sentences.zh: 建義初，遇害於河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he met disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he perished at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公、冀州刺史，追封武津縣公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Duke of the Secretariat and Inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Duke of the Secretariat and Inspector of Jizhou, enfeoffed Duke of Wujin County.

sentences.zh: 子瓚，字祖珍，位兼尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: His son Zan, style Zuzhen, held the concurrent post of Left Assistant in the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan, styled Zuzhen, served as concurrent Left Assistant of the Secretariat and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瓚妻，莊帝姊也，後封襄城長公主，故特贈瓚冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuangdi; later she was enfeoffed Princess of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially posthumously made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's wife was Emperor Zhuangdi's sister; later enfeoffed Princess of Xiangcheng, she secured Zan's posthumous appointment as Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子茂，字祖昂，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Mao, style Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao, styled Zu'ang, inherited the grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 邸珍，字安寶，本中山上曲陽人也，魏太和中，徙居武州鎮。

translations.literal: Di Zhen, style Anbao, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan; in the Taihe era of Wei he moved to reside at Wuzhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Di Zhen, styled Anbao, came from Shangquyang in Zhongshan; in Wei's Taihe era his family moved to Wuzhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，六鎮兵起，珍遂從杜洛周賊。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the Six Garrisons rose in arms; Zhen then followed the bandit Du Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons rebelled in the Xiaochang era he followed the rebel Du Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 洛周為葛榮所吞，珍入榮軍。

translations.literal: Luozhou was swallowed by Ge Rong; Zhen entered Rong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong, and Zhen entered Rong's army.

sentences.zh: 榮為爾硃榮所破，珍與其餘黨，俱徙并州。

translations.literal: Rong was broken by Erzhu Rong; Zhen and the remaining band went together to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was broken by Erzhu Rong, Zhen and the remnant fled to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從齊神武出山東。

translations.literal: He followed Qi Shenwu east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Qi Shenwu into Shandong.

sentences.zh: 神武起義信都，拜珍長史，封上曲縣侯，除殷州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shenwu raised righteousness at Xindu, Zhen was appointed Chief Clerk, enfeoffed Marquis of Shangqu County, and made Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu raised his banner at Xindu, Zhen became Chief Clerk, was enfeoffed Marquis of Shangqu, and made Inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 珍求取無厭，大為州人所疾苦。

translations.literal: Zhen's demands were insatiable; the people of the province suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's exactions were insatiable and the province groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射、大行台，節度諸軍事，擊梁州將成景攜等，解東行圍，回軍彭城。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Commissioner, directing all military affairs; he attacked Liang general Cheng Jingxi and the like, relieved the siege of Dongxing, and returned the army to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as concurrent Right Vice Director and Grand Commissioner, he directed armies against Liang's Cheng Jingxi, lifted the siege of Dongxing, and withdrew to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 珍禦下殘酷，士眾離心，至於土人豪族，遇之無禮，遂為州人所害。

translations.literal: Zhen was cruel to those below; soldiers and masses lost heart; even local magnates he treated without ritual, and the people of the province killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel to subordinates, he alienated troops and gentry alike until the provincials killed him.

sentences.zh: 後贈定州刺史、司空公。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of the Works.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Inspector of Dingzhou and Duke of the Works.

sentences.zh: 田式，字顯標，馮翊下邽人也。

translations.literal: Tian Shi, style Xianbiao, was a man of Xiaji in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shi, styled Xianbiao, came from Xiaji in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 祖安興、父長樂，仕魏，俱為本郡太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Anxing and father Changle both served Wei as prefects of their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anxing and father Changle had both served Wei as native prefects.

sentences.zh: 式性剛果，多武藝，拳勇絕人。

translations.literal: Shi's nature was firm and resolute; he had many martial arts, and his fists and courage surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was resolute, skilled in many martial arts, and unmatched in raw strength.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位渭南太守，政尚嚴猛，吏人重足而立，無敢違法。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was prefect of Weinan; his government prized severity, clerks and people stood as if on tiptoe, and none dared violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he governed Weinan with harsh severity; clerks and commoners trembled and dared not break the law.

sentences.zh: 遷本郡太守，親故屏跡，請托不行。

translations.literal: Transferred to be prefect of his native commandery, kin and friends withdrew their tracks and requests for favor went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to his home commandery, kin and friends ceased their petitions and favors went nowhere.

sentences.zh: 周武帝聞而善之，進位儀同三司，賜爵信都縣公，擢拜延州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou heard and approved, advanced him to Pillar of State, third rank, enfeoffed him Duke of Xindu County, and promoted him Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou praised him, raised him to Pillar of State, third rank, enfeoffed him Duke of Xindu, and made him Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，以功授上開府，徙為建州刺史，改封梁泉縣公。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Qi, by merit he was made Upper Opening-Fu, transferred to Inspector of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Qi he was made Upper Opening-Fu, transferred to Jianzhou, and enfeoffed Duke of Liangquan.

sentences.zh: 後從韋孝寬討尉遲迥，以功拜大將軍，進爵武山郡公。

translations.literal: Later he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yu Chi Tong; by merit he was made Great General and advanced to Duke of Wushan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yu Chi Tong, was made Great General, and advanced to Duke of Wushan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝受禪，拜襄州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was appointed General-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne he was appointed general-in-chief of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 專以立威為務，每視事於外，必盛氣以待之。

translations.literal: He devoted himself solely to establishing awe; whenever he held court outside he must display fierce spirit to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled solely by terror, always receiving audiences abroad in full martial display.

sentences.zh: 其下官屬，股栗無敢仰視。

translations.literal: His subordinate officials, thighs trembling, did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates shook with fear and dared not raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 有犯禁者，雖至親昵，無所容貸。

translations.literal: Whoever violated prohibitions, even the most intimate, received no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Even intimates who broke the law received no mercy.

sentences.zh: 其女婿京兆杜甯自長安省之，式誡寧無出外。

translations.literal: His son-in-law Du Ning of the capital came from Chang'an to visit; Shi warned Ning not to go outside.
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Du Ning of Chang'an came to visit; Shi forbade him to leave the compound.

sentences.zh: 寧久之不得還，竊上北樓，以暢羈思。

translations.literal: Ning long could not return; he secretly climbed the north tower to ease his longing.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to return for a long time, Ning secretly climbed the north tower to ease his longing.

sentences.zh: 式知之，杖寧五十。

translations.literal: Shi learned of it and flogged Ning fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Shi discovered it and flogged him fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 其所愛奴，嘗詣式白事，有蟲上其衣衿，揮袖拂去之，式以為慢己，立棒殺之。

translations.literal: A favorite slave once came to report to Shi; a bug climbed his collar and he flicked his sleeve to brush it away; Shi thought this slighted him and at once clubbed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: A favorite slave reporting business brushed an insect from his collar; Shi deemed it insolent and clubbed him dead on the spot.

sentences.zh: 或僚吏奸贓，部內劫盜者，無問輕重，悉禁地阱中，寢處糞穢，令受苦毒。

translations.literal: If clerks were corrupt or bandits robbed within the district, regardless of severity all were imprisoned in a pit in the earth, slept amid filth and dung, and were made to suffer bitter poison.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks and local robbers alike, whatever the offense, were thrown into earthen pits amid filth to suffer torment.

sentences.zh: 自非身死，終不得出。

translations.literal: Unless they died in person they could never come out.
translations.idiomatic: None left alive except by death.

sentences.zh: 每赦書到州，式未暇省讀，先召獄卒殺重囚，然後宣示百姓。

translations.literal: Whenever an amnesty edict reached the province, Shi had no leisure to read it; he first summoned jailers to kill the heavy criminals, then proclaimed it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesty edicts arrived he did not read them first but ordered jailers to execute the worst prisoners, then announced the edict to the people.

sentences.zh: 其刻暴如此。

translations.literal: His harsh cruelty was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his savagery.

sentences.zh: 由是為上所譴，除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reprimanded by the emperor and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reprimanded him and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 式慚恚不食，妻子至其所輒怒，唯侍僮二人，給使左右。

translations.literal: Shi, ashamed and resentful, would not eat; when wife and children came to his place he grew angry, and only two serving boys attended him left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and furious, he refused food; when wife and children approached he raged, keeping only two servant boys.

sentences.zh: 從家中索椒，欲自殺，家人不與。

translations.literal: He sought pepper from the house to kill himself; the family would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded pepper from the household to poison himself; the family refused.

sentences.zh: 陰遣侍僮詣市買毒藥，妻子又奪棄之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent the serving boys to the market to buy poison; his wife again seized and discarded it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent the boys to buy poison; his wife seized and discarded it.

sentences.zh: 式恚臥，其子信時為儀同，至式前流涕曰：「大人既是朝廷重臣，又無大過，比見公卿放辱者多矣，旋復外用，大人何能久乎？

translations.literal: Shi lay in resentment; his son Xin, at the time a Pillar of State, came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are already a heavy minister of the court and have no great offense; lately many public men have been shamed and released, then soon employed again abroad—how can you endure so long?"
translations.idiomatic: Lying in fury, his son Xin, then a Pillar of State, wept before him: "Father, you are a great minister without grave fault; many disgraced officials have soon been restored—why must you endure so long?"

sentences.zh: 乃至於此！

translations.literal: Even to this!"
translations.idiomatic: To come to such an extreme!"

sentences.zh: 」式欻起抽刀斫信，信避之，刃中於門。

translations.literal: Shi suddenly rose, drew a knife, and hacked at Xin; Xin dodged, and the blade struck the door.
translations.idiomatic: Shi leapt up and slashed at Xin; Xin dodged and the blade struck the door.

sentences.zh: 上知之，以式為罪己之深，復其官爵，尋拜廣州總管，卒官。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it; because Shi's guilt toward himself was deep, he restored his office and title, and soon appointed him General-in-Chief of Guangzhou, dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, judging his self-reproach sufficient, restored rank and soon appointed him general-in-chief of Guangzhou, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 燕榮，字貴公，華陰弘農人也。

translations.literal: Yan Rong, style Guigong, was a man of Hongnong in Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rong, styled Guigong, came from Hongnong in Huayin.

sentences.zh: 父侃，周大將軍榮性剛嚴，有武藝。

translations.literal: Father Kan was a great general of Zhou; Rong's nature was firm and stern and he had martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan was a Zhou great general; Rong was stern and martial.

sentences.zh: 仕周，為內侍上士。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he was a Superior Attendant of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as superior attendant of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 從武帝伐齊，以功授開府儀同三司，封高邑縣公。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in attacking Qi, by merit he was made Opening-Fu with equal ceremony to the third rank and enfeoffed Duke of Gaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Qi with Emperor Wu, he was made Opening-Fu of the third rank and enfeoffed Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進位大將軍，進封落叢郡公，拜晉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was advanced to Great General, his enfeoffment raised to Duke of Luocong Commandery, and he was appointed Inspector of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne he was made Great General, advanced to Duke of Luocong Commandery, and appointed inspector of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋從河間王弘擊突厥，以功拜上柱國，遷青州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Prince Hejian Hong in attacking the Turks; by merit he was made Pillar of State and transferred to General-in-Chief of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Prince Hejian Hong against the Turks, was made Pillar of State, and transferred to general-in-chief of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州，選絕有力者為伍伯。

translations.literal: In the province he selected the strongest men to be ward chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he chose the strongest men as ward chiefs.

sentences.zh: 吏人過之者，必加詰問，輒楚撻之，創多見骨。

translations.literal: When clerks and people passed them, he always interrogated them further and at once flogged them; wounds often showed bone.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone passing them was interrogated and flogged until wounds often showed bone.

sentences.zh: 奸盜屏跡，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Traitors and robbers withdrew their tracks; within the borders all was austere.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves vanished and the province grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 他州縣人經其界者，畏若寇仇，不敢休息。

translations.literal: People of other prefectures and counties who passed through his borders feared him as a bitter foe and dared not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers from other districts feared his borders as enemy country and dared not pause.

sentences.zh: 後因入朝覲，特加恩遇。

translations.literal: Later, because he entered court for an audience, he received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gained special favor on entering court.

sentences.zh: 榮以母老，請每歲入朝，上許之。

translations.literal: Rong, because his mother was old, asked to enter court each year; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Citing an aged mother, he asked to attend court yearly and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，以為行軍總管，率水軍自東萊傍海入太湖，取吳郡。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was made campaigning general-in-chief, leading the water army from Donglai along the sea into Tai Lake to take Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chen campaign he commanded the fleet from Donglai along the coast into Tai Lake to seize Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 既破丹陽，吳人共立蕭瓛，為宇文述所敗，退保包山。

translations.literal: After Danyang was broken, the Wu people together set up Xiao Xian; he was defeated by Yuwen Shu and retreated to hold Baoshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Danyang fell the Wu set up Xiao Xian; defeated by Yuwen Shu, Xian retreated to Baoshan.

sentences.zh: 榮率精甲躡之，瓛敗走，為榮所執。

translations.literal: Rong led elite armor in pursuit; Xian was defeated and fled and was captured by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong pursued with elite troops, captured the fleeing Xian, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 事平，檢校揚州總管。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made acting Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification he was acting inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為武候將軍，後除幽州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Martial-House General and later made General-in-Chief of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned as Martial-House General, he later became general-in-chief of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮性嚴酷，有威容，長吏見者，莫不惶懼自失。

translations.literal: Rong's nature was stern and cruel, with a fearsome countenance; long officials who saw him all lost themselves in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and cruel, with a fearsome face, he made senior officials tremble at sight.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧氏，世為著姓，榮皆署為吏卒，以屈辱之。

translations.literal: The Lu clan of Fanyang, for generations a noted surname, Rong all appointed as clerks and runners to humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: The eminent Lu clan of Fanyang he reduced to clerks and runners to humiliate them.

sentences.zh: 鞭笞左右，動至千數，流血盈前，飲啖自若。

translations.literal: Flogging those at his side reached thousands; blood overflowed before him yet he drank and ate as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He flogged attendants by the thousand until blood pooled before him, yet ate and drank calmly.

sentences.zh: 嘗按部，道次見叢荊，堪為笞箠，命取之，輒以試人。

translations.literal: Once on inspection, passing thorn bushes fit for the lash, he ordered them taken and at once tried them on people.
translations.idiomatic: On tour he saw thorn brush fit for scourging, had it cut, and tested it on passersby.

sentences.zh: 人或自陳無咎，榮曰：'後有罪，當免。

translations.literal: If someone declared himself without fault, Rong said: 'Later when there is guilt, it shall be remitted.'
translations.idiomatic: If a man protested innocence Rong said, "If you offend later, I will spare you."

sentences.zh: 」及後犯細過，將撾之，人曰：「前日被杖，許有罪宥之。

translations.literal: Later when he committed a small offense and was about to flog him, the man said: "The other day when I was beaten you promised guilt would be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: When the man later erred and was to be beaten, he said, "You promised pardon when you beat me before."

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「無過尚爾，況有過邪！

translations.literal: Rong said: "When there was no fault it was still thus—how much more when there is fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "I beat you when you were innocent—how much more now that you are guilty!"

sentences.zh: 」榜捶如舊。

translations.literal: The cudgel blows were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The beating proceeded as before.

sentences.zh: 榮每巡省管內，聞人吏妻有美色，輒舍其室而淫之，貪暴放縱日甚。

translations.literal: Whenever Rong inspected his jurisdiction and heard that a clerk or commoner's wife was beautiful, he would leave his quarters and violate her; greed and violence grew more unrestrained daily.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection he raped any beautiful wife he heard of among clerks or commoners; greed and violence grew daily.

sentences.zh: 時元弘嗣除幽州長史，懼辱，固辭。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Hongsi was made Chief Clerk of Youzhou; fearing humiliation, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hongsi became chief clerk of Youzhou he declined firmly, fearing disgrace.

sentences.zh: 上知之，敕榮曰：「弘嗣杖十已上罪，皆奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and ordered Rong: "For Hongsi, offenses warranting ten strokes or more must all be reported."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Rong, "Report every offense of Hongsi warranting ten strokes or more."

sentences.zh: 」榮忿曰：「豎子何敢弄我！

translations.literal: Rong said in anger: "How dare the stripling toy with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong raged, "How dare that stripling play with me!"

sentences.zh: 」及遣弘嗣監納倉粟，颺得一糠一秕，罰之，每笞不滿十，然一日中或至三數。

translations.literal: He sent Hongsi to supervise the collection of granary grain; a single husk or chaff was blown up—he punished him, each flogging not reaching ten, yet in one day there might be several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He set Hongsi to oversee granary grain; one husk blown astray brought a beating—never ten strokes, yet several dozen in a day.

sentences.zh: 如是歷年，怨隙日構。

translations.literal: Thus for years; resentment daily built.
translations.idiomatic: For years resentment mounted.

sentences.zh: 榮遂收付獄，禁絕其糧。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon seized him and put him in prison, cutting off his food.
translations.idiomatic: Rong seized him, imprisoned him, and cut off food.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣饑，抽衣絮雜水咽之。

translations.literal: Hongsi, starving, pulled out cotton from his clothes, mixed it with water, and swallowed it.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, Hongsi swallowed cotton padding soaked in water.

sentences.zh: 其妻詣闕稱冤，上遣考功侍郎劉士龍馳驛鞫問，奏榮毒虐，又贓穢狼籍，遂征還京，賜死。

translations.literal: His wife went to the palace to proclaim her wrong; the emperor sent Reviewing Officer Liu Shilong on post-horses to interrogate quickly; he reported Rong's poisonous cruelty and also bribes in heaps, and Rong was summoned back to the capital and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife appealed at court; the emperor sent Reviewing Officer Liu Shilong by relay horse; Rong was found cruel and corrupt, recalled, and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 先是，榮家寢室無故有蛆數斛從地墳出。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Rong's sleeping chamber for no reason maggots in several hu welled up from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier maggots had welled by the bushel from the floor of his bedchamber without cause.

sentences.zh: 未幾，榮死於蛆出之處。

translations.literal: Before long Rong died at the place where the maggots had emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died where the maggots had appeared.

sentences.zh: 有子詢。

translations.literal: He had a son Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son Xun.

sentences.zh: 元弘嗣

translations.literal: Yuan Hongsi
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi

sentences.zh: 元弘嗣，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongsi was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongsi came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖剛，魏漁陽王。

translations.literal: Grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父經，周漁陽郡公。

translations.literal: Father Jing was Duke of Yuyang Commandery of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing was Duke of Yuyang Commandery under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣少襲爵，十八為左親衛。

translations.literal: Hongsi in youth inherited the title; at eighteen he was Left Personal Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited young, and at eighteen became Left Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，從晉王平陳，以功授上儀同。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he followed the Prince of Jin in pacifying Chen; by merit he was made Upper Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang's first year he followed the Prince of Jin against Chen and was made Upper Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 後除觀州長史，以嚴峻任事，州人多怨之。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk of Guanzhou; because he was stern and severe in affairs, many in the province resented him.
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk of Guanzhou his stern rule bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 轉幽州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 時總管燕榮肆虐於弘嗣，每笞辱。

translations.literal: At the time the general-in-chief Yan Rong ran riot against Hongsi, flogging and humiliating him at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: There the general-in-chief Yan Rong abused him with constant beatings.

sentences.zh: 弘嗣心不伏，遂被禁。

translations.literal: Hongsi's heart would not submit; he was thereupon imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Unbowed, he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 及榮誅，弘嗣為政，酷又甚之。

translations.literal: When Rong was executed, Hongsi took power; his cruelty was again even greater.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's execution Hongsi took power and proved even crueler.

sentences.zh: 每鞫囚，多以酢灌鼻，或椓弋其下竅。

translations.literal: Whenever he interrogated prisoners he often poured vinegar into the nose, or drove stakes into the lower orifice.
translations.idiomatic: He interrogated by pouring vinegar into prisoners' noses or driving stakes into their lower bodies.

sentences.zh: 無敢隱情，奸偽屏息。

translations.literal: None dared hide the facts; treachery and falsehood ceased.
translations.idiomatic: None dared conceal guilt; deceit vanished.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，授木工監，修營東都。

translations.literal: At the end of the Renshou era he was appointed Director of the Carpentry Office to build the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era he directed carpentry for the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 大業初，煬帝潛有遼東意，遣弘嗣於東萊海口監造船。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era Emperor Yang secretly had designs on Liaodong and sent Hongsi to Donglai Harbor to supervise shipbuilding.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's opening Emperor Yang secretly planned Liaodong and sent Hongsi to Donglai to supervise shipbuilding.

sentences.zh: 諸州役丁苦其捶楚，官人當作，晝夜立水中，略不敢息，自腰已下無不蛆生，死者十三四。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers of the provinces suffered his beatings; officials on duty stood day and night in the water, scarcely daring to rest; from the waist down none failed to breed maggots, and thirteen or fourteen in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée workers suffered his lash; overseers stood day and night in water to their waists, breeding maggots; thirteen or fourteen in ten died.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎，轉殿中少監。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Vice Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then vice director of the palace.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後奴賊寇隴西，詔弘嗣擊之。

translations.literal: Later when slave bandits raided Longxi, an edict ordered Hongsi to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When slave rebels raided Longxi he was ordered to attack.

sentences.zh: 及玄感反，弘嗣屯兵安定。

translations.literal: When Xuan'gan rebelled, Hongsi encamped troops at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuan'gan rebelled he encamped at Anding.

sentences.zh: 或告之謀應玄感，代王侑遣執送行在所。

translations.literal: Someone reported that he plotted to respond to Xuan'gan; the Prince of Dai You had him seized and sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of joining Yang Xuan'gan, he was seized by the Prince of Dai and sent to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 以無反釋。

translations.literal: Because there was no rebellion he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Found innocent of rebellion, he was released.

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，除名徙日南，道死。

translations.literal: The emperor still suspected him, struck his name from the rolls, and exiled him to Rinan; he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Still suspecting him, the emperor struck his name and exiled him to Rinan, where he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 有子仁觀。

translations.literal: He had a son Renguan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son Renguan.

sentences.zh: 王文同

translations.literal: Wang Wentong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentong

sentences.zh: 王文同，京兆頻陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wentong was a man of Pinyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wentong came from Pinyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性明辯，有幹用。

translations.literal: By nature clear in debate, he had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sharp in debate and capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，以軍功拜儀同，授桂州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era, by military merit he was made Pillar of State with equal ceremony and appointed Marshal of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang, by military merit he became Pillar of State and marshal of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，為光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was made Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he became vice director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 以忤旨，出為恆山郡贊務。

translations.literal: Because he offended the emperor's intent, he was sent out as Assistant Administrator of Hengshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Offending the throne, he was sent out as assistant administrator of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 有一人豪猾，每持長吏長短，前後守令咸憚之。

translations.literal: There was a man fierce and slippery who always held the faults of senior officials; successive prefects and magistrates all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce local bully always held magistrates' secrets in fear.

sentences.zh: 文同下車，聞其名而數之。

translations.literal: When Wentong took his post he heard the name and repeatedly reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Wentong heard of him and rebuked him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 因令剡木為大橛，埋之於庭，出尺餘，四面各埋小橛，令其人踣心於木橛上，縛四支於小橛，以棒打其背，應時潰爛。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered a great stake carved from wood buried in the courtyard, projecting more than a foot, with small stakes buried on four sides; he made the man lie heart-down on the great stake, bound his four limbs to the small stakes, and beat his back with a club until it promptly putrefied.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a great wooden stake for the courtyard, bound the man spread-eagled upon it, and beat his back until it burst open.

sentences.zh: 郡中大駭，吏人懾氣。

translations.literal: The whole commandery was greatly shocked; clerks and people were cowed.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was horrified; clerks and people trembled.

sentences.zh: 及帝征遼東，令文同巡察河北諸郡，文同見沙門齋戒菜食者，以為妖妄，皆收系之。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned on Liaodong he ordered Wentong to inspect the commanderies of Hebei; Wentong saw monks fasting on vegetables and regarded them as demonic delusion, all seizing and binding them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he inspected Hebei; seeing monks on vegetable fasts he seized them as sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 北至河間，召郡官人。

translations.literal: Going north to Hejian he summoned the commandery's officials.
translations.idiomatic: North at Hejian he summoned the officials.

sentences.zh: 小有遲違者，輒覆面於地而捶殺之。

translations.literal: Whoever was slightly tardy he at once covered the face to the ground and beat them to death.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest delay brought a face-down beating to death.

sentences.zh: 求沙門相聚講論及長老共為佛會者數百人，文同以為聚結惑眾，盡斬之。

translations.literal: He found several hundred monks gathered to discuss doctrine and elders jointly holding Buddhist assemblies; Wentong regarded this as gathering the masses to delude the people and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Finding hundreds at Buddhist assemblies he beheaded them as sedition.

sentences.zh: 又悉裸僧尼，驗有淫狀非童男女者數千人，復將殺之。

translations.literal: He also stripped monks and nuns bare, examined those with signs of licentious conduct and not virgin boys and girls—several thousand—and was about to kill them again.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped monks and nuns, found thousands with signs of sexual misconduct, and prepared another massacre.

sentences.zh: 郡中士女，號哭於路，諸郡驚駭，各奏其事。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and ladies of the commandery wailed along the roads; the commanderies were shocked and each memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wailed in the streets; terrified districts each memorialized the horror.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，遣使者違奚善意馳鎖之，斬於河間，以謝百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor heard, was greatly enraged, and sent envoy Wei Yishanyi on post-horses to shackle him and behead him at Hejian to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged, sent Wei Yishanyi by relay horse to shackle and behead him at Hejian to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 仇人剖其棺，臠其肉啖之，斯須咸盡。

translations.literal: Enemies opened his coffin, sliced his flesh, and ate it; in an instant it was all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies opened his coffin, ate his flesh, and devoured it in moments.

translations.literal: Discussion
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 論曰：士之立名，其途不一，或以循良進，或以嚴酷顯。

translations.literal: The discussion says: For a gentleman to establish a name, the paths are not one; some advance by gentleness and goodness, some stand forth by severity and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes that men make names by different roads—some by humane governance, some by pitiless severity.

sentences.zh: 故寬猛相資，德刑互設。

translations.literal: Therefore leniency and severity assist each other; virtue and punishment are set in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency and severity must complement each other; moral sway and penal law alternate.

sentences.zh: 然不嚴而化，君子所先。

translations.literal: Yet to transform without severity is what the gentleman puts first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet civilizing without harshness remains the gentleman's first choice.

sentences.zh: 于洛侯等為惡不同，同歸於酷，肆其毒螫，多行殘忍。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou and the rest did evil in different ways but alike returned to cruelty, unleashing their poisonous stings and often acting with savage cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou and his like sinned in different ways yet alike in cruelty, stinging like vipers and delighting in savagery.

sentences.zh: 賤人肌膚，同諸木石；

translations.literal: They despised men's flesh as they would wood and stone;
translations.idiomatic: They treated human flesh like wood and stone;

sentences.zh: 輕人性命，甚於芻狗。

translations.literal: they held men's lives lighter than grass and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: they held life cheaper than straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及。

translations.literal: Long persisting in evil without repentance, few failed to reach the end.
translations.idiomatic: Persisting in evil, few escaped retribution.

sentences.zh: 故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚俱殞，異術皆斃，各其宜焉。

translations.literal: Therefore some personally received punishment and execution, some died of grief and resentment together; different fates alike perished, each as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Some died by the law, some by grief and rage; diverse ends alike consumed them, each as he deserved.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道矣。

translations.literal: All gentlemen of principle hold that Heaven's Way was at work.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle see in this the working of Heaven's Way.
